interface.title: Spike Doctor
interface.stage_of_work: Primary analysis of raw recordings: spike detection, feature extraction, QC and export
interface.what_it_is_for: Load one or more ABF current-clamp recordings, detect action potentials in each current-step sweep using voltage and dV/dt thresholds, extract eFEL electrophysiological features, review F-I curves, phase-plane plots and per-sweep debug traces, and export the results as CSV, Excel or PDF.

data.note: patch-clamp-current-steps.abf: ABF 2.0, protocol 'step cclamp', 1 channel, 9 sweeps of 1 s at 20 kHz, steps from -100 to +300 pA in 50 pA increments. With defaults, sweeps 6/7/8 (200/250/300 pA) fire 2/2/3 spikes and rheobase is 200 pA. To test multi-file analysis, the same file was uploaded twice, because no second test file was available.

features.name: Amplitude-threshold event detection with live re-analysis
features.general: Set an amplitude cut-off for counting events; every edit re-runs detection, and the counts, response curve and per-trial overlays update
features.specific: Edit Detection Threshold (mV) in the sidebar; the Analysis Summary echoes the setting and the Spike Count vs Current plot, table and Debug plot threshold line all refresh. The neighbouring Derivative Threshold (mV/ms) is accepted and echoed, but raising it from 10 to 400 mV/ms left spike counts unchanged (screens/024-026)
steps: Type a new Detection Threshold, e.g. 33 mV
Leave the field (Tab) to trigger re-analysis
Check the 'Current Settings' block in the Analysis Summary
Check the F-I curve and spike_count column for changed counts
Open Debug Plots to see the new threshold line and which peaks are marked
serves_tasks: Raise or lower the amplitude cut-off for counting an event

features.name: Per-trial detection inspector with sweep slider
features.general: Scrub through trials with a slider and, for each one, see the raw trace with detected events, the threshold and baseline lines, and the stimulus waveform with the analysis window shaded; with several recordings, the same trial is shown for each side by side
features.specific: Debug Plots tab: the Debug Sweep slider (0 to 8, drag or arrow keys) redraws a two-panel plot per file: voltage with red spike markers, the detection-threshold and V_base lines and a 'Spikes: n' legend, over the command current with the stimulus epoch shaded. Caveat: the legend read 'Spikes: 1' on sweep 4, where no spike is marked (screens/036.webp); the reviewer traced it to counting eFEL peak times rather than spikes inside the stimulus window, so count the red markers instead
steps: Open the Debug Plots tab
Drag the Debug Sweep slider or press the arrow keys to pick a sweep
Count the red spike markers against the threshold line (do not rely on the legend count)
Compare the panels of each uploaded file at the same sweep
serves_tasks: Analyse several recordings in one batch

features.name: Stimulus-response summary panel (traces, F-I curve, phase plane)
features.general: For each recording, show three linked summaries: all trials overlaid, response count against stimulus amplitude, and a phase-plane plot (rate of voltage change against voltage) at a reference stimulus; a 'not found' state appears when no responding trial exists
features.specific: Summary Plots > File Plots: Raw sweep overlay, Spike Count vs Current (F-I) and Phase Plane Plot at 2x Rheobase (dV/dt vs Vm), one row per file; a wrong Stimulus Epoch Index gives a flat F-I and 'Rheobase Not Found'. Rheobase and F-I slope are not printed as numbers
steps: Upload one or more ABF files
Scroll to File Plots on the Summary Plots tab
Read off the plot the lowest current that fires and how spike count rises with current
Check the phase-plane loop at 2x rheobase
Change Stimulus Epoch Index if the F-I curve is empty
serves_tasks: Plot firing against stimulus strength and check spike shape
Choose which part of the protocol counts as the stimulus
Analyse several recordings in one batch

features.name: Searchable feature picker (Basic / Advanced)
features.general: Choose measurements from a short curated list or a full searchable catalogue; the selection sets the output columns. Known bug: changing the search text silently drops ticked items it hides
features.specific: 'eFEL Features to Calculate': the Basic tab has 8 named checkboxes; the Advanced tab has a 'Filter features' box over 174 eFEL feature checkboxes with a 'Showing n of 174' count; the selection count appears in the summary as '# eFEL Features Selected' and as table columns. Changing the filter text unticked spike_half_width once it was hidden (count 7 to 6, column gone, screens/047.webp), and a click during the list redraw can fail to register
steps: Pick the Basic or Advanced tab
In Advanced, type part of a feature name in Filter features
Tick or untick feature checkboxes
Check the '# eFEL Features Selected' count and the table columns, since earlier ticks may have been dropped by a filter change

features.name: Combined results grid with sorting
features.general: One long table of per-trial and per-event measurements across all loaded recordings, sortable by any column
features.specific: Detailed Results Table > Combined Analysis Data: a scrolling grid with filename, sweep, current_step_pA and event_index plus one column per feature; click a header to sort; the footer shows 'Viewing rows x through y of N'. Per-spike rows (event_index > 0) appear only when a per-spike feature such as spike_half_width is selected; otherwise there is one row per sweep
steps: Open the Detailed Results Table tab
Scroll vertically and horizontally through the rows and feature columns
Click a column header (e.g. spike_count) to sort
serves_tasks: Read per-trial measurements in a table
Analyse several recordings in one batch

features.name: Multi-format results export
features.general: Download the current results as a flat table, a workbook or a figure report; the buttons only appear once an analysis has succeeded
features.specific: Sidebar: Download Results (CSV), Download Results (Excel) and Download Summary Plots (PDF, '2 files per A4 page'); file names carry the file count and a timestamp; after a failed analysis the buttons are replaced by 'Upload and analyse files to enable downloads.' Excel and PDF contents were not viewed
steps: Run an analysis that succeeds
Press the CSV, Excel or PDF button
Open the timestamped download

features.name: Analysis Summary / run-status panel
features.general: A status block that reports how many files were analysed or failed, echoes the current settings and lists what was computed, so a run can be checked before its results are trusted
features.specific: Analysis Summary on the Summary Plots tab: 'Successfully Analyzed' and 'Analysis Skipped/Failed' counts, a 'Current Settings' block (e.g. Spike V Threshold), '# eFEL Features Selected' and the Output Columns list, alongside the ABF file details

Scroll to the Analysis Summary on the Summary Plots tab
Check the success/failure counts
Check that Current Settings and '# eFEL Features Selected' match what you intended

screens_never_reached: The Excel sheets and PDF pages: the downloads are binary and could only be confirmed by file name and size (xlsx 10.7 KB, PDF 171 KB). Their contents were not viewed.

An Analysis Logs view with newer entries: the panel kept showing the same first 9 lines (a WARN, two INFOs, then eFEL mean_frequency warnings for sweeps 0–5) after later re-analyses, including the channel-1 failure, so no log of that failure was seen (screens/030.webp).
not_done: Using the derivative threshold to reject noise did not show any effect. Raising Derivative Threshold from 10 to 250 and then 400 mV/ms was applied (summary reads 250 mV/ms) but left the spike counts unchanged at 0/0/0/0/0/0/2/2/3 (screens/024.webp, screens/025.webp, screens/026.webp). In this tool it does not appear to filter the spike count.
Clear Logs: pressing it left the log text unchanged (screens/013.webp, screens/014.webp).

Comparing genuinely different recordings: only one test file exists, so the multi-file run used two copies of it. Both copies carry the same filename in the table and CSV, so rows from different files cannot be told apart unless the files have different names.

Selection is lost when the filter changes: in the Advanced feature list, changing the filter text silently dropped a ticked feature (spike_half_width) that was now hidden. The count went from 7 to 6 and the column disappeared (screens/047.webp). A click during the list's redraw also failed to register, so ISI_CV had to be ticked twice.
ISI_CV values: the column appeared after ticking it (screens/049.webp), but its values were not checked on the spiking sweeps.

Debug legend count is unreliable: on sweep 4, where no spike is marked, the legend reads 'Spikes: 1' (screens/036.webp). The replay agent also suspected this but could not read it clearly; the reviewer traced it to the legend counting eFEL peak times rather than spikes inside the stimulus window.
